newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore politician calls on Lee to quit over row.
newsitem.headline: Singapore politician calls on Lee to quit over row.

text.p: An opposition politician has said Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew, at the centre of a row with Malaysia, should resign for damaging relations between the two countries.

"It is time for Lee to leave the cabinet so that he can no longer embarass the Singapore people as well as damage the existing good relations between the two countries," the politician, Tang Liang Hong, told reporters at a briefing on Friday in the Malaysian state of Johor across from Singapore.
"I think he is a man of the past. His mentality, his attitude still stays in the period of the cold war," Tang said in remarks published by Singapore's Straits Times newspaper on Saturday.
There was no immediate comment from the Singapore government.
The row first erupted after Lee described Johor in a court affidavit as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings."

Malaysians reacted angrily, with members of the youth wing of the ruling UMNO party of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad calling Lee, who had led Singapore until stepping down in 1990, "senile", and Malaysia's foreign minister calling for an apology and a retraction.

Lee apologised and instructed his lawyer to ask the court to remove the remarks from the affidavit, filed in relation to a libel suit against Tang, who lost a hotly contested race in the January 2 elections in Singapore and fled to Johor after claiming he had received death threats.

After Kuala Lumpur accepted Lee's apology, the row flared up again last Thursday when Malaysia's state-run news agency Bernama and its major newspapers said the country was freezing new bilateral dealings with Singapore.
The reports were denied later, with Malaysia saying it wanted the dispute to end but that the city-state's leaders should show some earnestness in rebuilding ties.
Tang also called on Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong to have his government take responsibility for Lee's actions.
"As a political leader, you can't say that it has nothing to do with the cabinet, especially if he (Lee) is the next most important member (of the government) after himself," Tang said.
"As a Singaporean, I say it is shameful that our country is running along in such a limping duck fashion."
